chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurara who said:

Ammar asked (while I was with him) about a man who marries the promiscuous woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah). He said: There is no harm, and if the other marriage (permanent) is (also there), let him guard his door.

key_terms.الفَاجِرَة: The promiscuous woman (one known for fornication or sexual indiscretion)
key_terms.لَا بَأْس: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.لِيُحْصِنْ بَابَهُ: Let him guard his door (idiom for discretion or managing household affairs)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry a promiscuous woman in temporary marriage according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Isfahani’s chain within al-Istibsar, this hadith clarifies that temporary marriage (mut'ah) is not restricted solely to virtuous women, as Imam al-Sadiq permits it with a 'promiscuous' woman (al-fajirah) provided the man exercises discretion. The condition to 'guard his door' (yuhassin babahu) is interpreted by Shia jurists as a directive to maintain privacy and manage household dynamics, particularly if he is concurrently married permanently, thereby preventing public scandal or domestic conflict.
